text.p: Following are the main stories in Friday's Malaysian newspapers. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
ALL newspapers lead with Prime Minister Mahathir Mohamad's lashing out at "rogue" currency speculators and "anarchists" who have caused a currency crisis in Southeast Asia.
-- The Anti-Corruption Agency will get more powers under provisions tabled in Parliament to amend the Anti-Corruption Bill, said Deputy Prime Minister Anwar Ibrahim.
-- A meeting between key companies involved in the Bakun hydroelectric dam failed to resolve differences over the project's engineering, procurement and construction contract.
-- Malaysian Helicopter Services Bhd may want to pull out of Royal Air Cambodge if the open skies policy is adopted by Cambodia, said MHS chairman Tajudin Ramli.
-- KUB Malaysia Bhd expects to be listed on the Kuala Lumpur Stock Exchange after several delays to its plans, said company chairman and CEO Hassan Harun.
